title: 2016 AMC 10A Problem 12
statement: Three distinct integers are selected at random between \(1\) and \(2016,\) inclusive. Which of the following is a correct statement about the probability \(p\) that the product of the three integers is odd?

solutions.text:
The product is odd exactly when all three selected integers are odd. There are \(1008\) odd and \(1008\) even integers from \(1\) to \(2016\).

Because the integers are selected without replacement, \[p=\frac{1008}{2016}\cdot\frac{1007}{2015}\cdot\frac{1006}{2014}.\] The first factor is \(\frac12\), and each of the next two factors is slightly less than \(\frac12\). Therefore \(p<\frac18\).

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: The product is odd only if all three selected integers are odd
Sampling without replacement makes the probability slightly less than \((\frac{1}{2})^3\)
